#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the Dart SDK — cached, channel-aware provisioner for machine-factory
# leg sessions (gh-918).
#
# WHY: factory legs (dev/review/rework) on Dart repos had NO dart SDK on PATH —
# they could not run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check`, so they
# could neither see nor verify quality-gate violations (CRAP / method_size /
# format) and claimed success while violations stayed in place. Same pattern
# as the golden-test Flutter toolchain for fa legs: the SDK is cached per
# resolved version and exposed on PATH for the leg session, resolving the SAME
# channel (and pinned version, when CI pins one) the checked-out repo's
# quality workflow uses — the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `channel:`/`sdk:`
# inputs in `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The SDK itself downloads from the same
# dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart` uses, so leg-local gate output
# matches CI gate output.
#
# Version-aware like setup/fa.sh: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on
# mismatch — pool VMs keep a PERSISTENT $HOME, so a presence-only check lets
# an ancient binary shadow the requested toolchain forever.
#
# Usage:
#   dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]  # default: dart-lang/setup-dart detection, else stable
#   DART_VERSION=beta dart.sh
#   DART_INSTALL_DIR=... dart.sh         # default: ~/.dart-sdk (SDK lands at <dir>/dart-sdk)
#
# Network-free subcommands (unit-test surface — js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js):
#   dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|<version>]
#       print the resolved target/URL/layout as key=value — no download
#   dart.sh status
#       print installed=<version from the dart --version banner> ('' when absent)
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/_common.sh"

DART_ARCHIVE="https://storage.googleapis.com/dart-archive"
DART_INSTALL_DIR="${DART_INSTALL_DIR:-${HOME}/.dart-sdk}"
SDK_HOME="${DART_INSTALL_DIR}/dart-sdk"
SDK_BIN="${SDK_HOME}/bin"

# ── Platform ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# dart-archive bundle naming: dartsdk-<os>-<arch>-release.zip (x64/arm64).
os_arch() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) OS="macos" ;;
    Linux)  OS="linux" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported OS ($(uname -s)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    arm64|aarch64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
    x86_64)        ARCH="x64" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported arch ($(uname -m)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
}

# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Checks PATH first, then
# our own install dir — a cache-restored SDK is real even before its bin dir
# is registered on PATH.
installed_version() {
  local d=""
  if command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    d="$(command -v dart)"
  elif [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
  fi
  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([0-9][0-9.]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# Latest concrete version of a channel (dart-lang/setup-dart resolves "latest"
# through the same VERSION file).
channel_latest() {
  curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/$1/release/latest/VERSION" \
    | sed -n 's/.*"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# ── Quality-workflow detection ("same channel the repo's quality.yml uses") ──
# Scan the checked-out repo's workflows for the dart-lang/setup-dart step and
# read its with: inputs. Echoes "found|sdk|channel" (any field may be empty).
quality_detection() {
  local f kv found=0 sdk="" channel=""
  for f in "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yml "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yaml; do
    [ -f "${f}" ] || continue
    while IFS= read -r kv; do
      case "${kv}" in
        step=*)    found=1 ;;
        sdk=*)     if [ -n "${kv#sdk=}" ] && [ -z "${sdk}" ]; then sdk="${kv#sdk=}"; found=1; fi ;;
        channel=*) if [ -n "${kv#channel=}" ] && [ -z "${channel}" ]; then channel="${kv#channel=}"; found=1; fi ;;
      esac
    done <<EOF
$(awk -v sq="'" '
  /uses:[[:space:]]*dart-lang\/setup-dart/ { inb = 1; print "step=1"; next }
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*(name|uses|run):[[:space:]]/ { inb = 0 }
  inb && /sdk:/ {
    sub(/.*sdk:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "sdk=" $0
  }
  inb && /channel:/ {
    sub(/.*channel:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "channel=" $0
  }
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
EOF
  done
  echo "${found}|${sdk}|${channel}"
}

# ── Target resolution ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Precedence (sets TARGET/MODE/CHANNEL/VERSION/SOURCE):
#   1. explicit argument           → source=argument
#   2. DART_VERSION env            → source=environment
#   3. quality.yml sdk:/channel:   → source=quality workflow
#   4. stable                      → source=default
# A pinned version rides the DETECTED channel (setup-dart keeps using the
# channel for a full version), so leg output keeps matching CI exactly.
resolve_target() {
  local arg="${1:-}"
  TARGET="${arg:-${DART_VERSION:-}}"
  SOURCE="default"
  if [ -n "${arg}" ]; then
    SOURCE="argument"
  elif [ -n "${DART_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    SOURCE="environment"
  fi

  local det found det_sdk det_channel
  det="$(quality_detection)"
  found="${det%%|*}"; det="${det#*|}"
  det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"

  if [ -z "${TARGET}" ]; then
    [ "${found}" = "1" ] && SOURCE="quality workflow"
    # A quality-workflow `sdk:` pin IS a target — the leg runs the exact
    # version CI runs; its `channel:` (or stable) then carries the download.
    [ -n "${det_sdk}" ] && TARGET="${det_sdk}"
  fi

  case "${TARGET}" in
    ""|latest|stable|beta|dev)
      MODE="channel"
      CHANNEL="${TARGET}"
      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ] || [ "${CHANNEL}" = "latest" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_channel}"; fi
      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_sdk:+stable}"; fi
      [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ] && CHANNEL="stable"
      case "${CHANNEL}" in stable|beta|dev) ;; *) CHANNEL="stable" ;; esac
      VERSION=""
      ;;
    *)
      MODE="version"
      VERSION="${TARGET}"
      CHANNEL="${det_channel}"
      [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ] && CHANNEL="stable"
      case "${CHANNEL}" in stable|beta|dev) ;; *) CHANNEL="stable" ;; esac
      ;;
  esac
}

# concrete version is fetched at install time.
sdk_url() {
  local ver="${1:-${VERSION:-latest}}"
  [ -n "${ver}" ] || ver="latest"
  echo "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/${CHANNEL}/release/${ver}/sdk/dartsdk-${OS}-${ARCH}-release.zip"
}

print_plan() {
  if [ "${MODE}" = "version" ]; then
    echo "requested=${VERSION}"
  else
    echo "requested=${CHANNEL}"

  echo "mode=${MODE}"
  echo "channel=${CHANNEL}"
  echo "version=${VERSION:-latest}"
  echo "source=${SOURCE}"
  echo "install_dir=${DART_INSTALL_DIR}"
  echo "sdk_home=${SDK_HOME}"

extract_zip() {

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Common utilities shared by all setup scripts.
# Source this file — do not run it directly.

# ── OS / CI / Package manager detection ──────────────────────────────────────

detect_os() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) echo "macos" ;;
    Linux)  echo "linux" ;;
    *)      echo "unknown" ;;
  esac
}

detect_ci() {
  if   [ -n "${BITRISE_BUILD_NUMBER:-}" ]; then echo "bitrise"
  elif [ -n "${GITHUB_ACTIONS:-}" ];       then echo "github"
  elif [ -n "${BUILD_BUILDID:-}" ];        then echo "ado"
  elif [ -n "${GITLAB_CI:-}" ];            then echo "gitlab"
  else                                          echo "local"
  fi
}

detect_package_manager() {
  if   is_installed brew;    then echo "brew"
  elif is_installed apt-get; then echo "apt"
  else                            echo "none"
  fi
}

# ── PATH / env registration ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Add a directory to PATH — works for the current shell AND subsequent CI steps.
register_path() {
  local dir="$1"
  # Export immediately so the rest of this script can use the binary.
  export PATH="${dir}:${PATH}"

  # Persist to a temp file so parent install.sh can accumulate all paths
  echo "${dir}" >> /tmp/_registered_paths 2>/dev/null || true

  case "$(detect_ci)" in
    bitrise)
      # envman REPLACES the variable — pass the full cumulative PATH.
      command -v envman &>/dev/null \
        && envman add --key PATH --value "${PATH}" \
        || true
      ;;
    github)
      [ -n "${GITHUB_PATH:-}" ] && echo "${dir}" >> "${GITHUB_PATH}" || true
      ;;
    gitlab)
      [ -n "${GITLAB_ENV_PATH:-}" ] && echo "export PATH=\"${dir}:\$PATH\"" >> "${GITLAB_ENV_PATH}" || true
      ;;
    ado)
      echo "##vso[task.prependpath]${dir}"
      ;;
    local) ;;  # already exported above
  esac
}

# Export an env variable so subsequent CI steps can see it.
export_var() {
  local key="$1" value="$2"
  export "${key}=${value}"

  case "$(detect_ci)" in
    bitrise)
      command -v envman &>/dev/null \
        && envman add --key "${key}" --value "${value}" \
        || true
      ;;
    github)
      [ -n "${GITHUB_ENV:-}" ] && echo "${key}=${value}" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}" || true
      ;;
    gitlab)
      [ -n "${GITLAB_ENV_PATH:-}" ] && echo "export ${key}=\"${value}\"" >> "${GITLAB_ENV_PATH}" || true
      ;;
    ado)
      echo "##vso[task.setvariable variable=${key}]${value}"
      ;;
    local) ;;
  esac
}

# ── Helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

is_installed() { command -v "$1" &>/dev/null; }

# Returns "sudo" when not running as root, empty string when already root.
# Usage: $(sudo_cmd) apt-get install ...
sudo_cmd() {
  if [ "$(id -u)" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "sudo"
  else
    echo ""
  fi
}

section() { echo ""; echo "▶ $*"; echo ""; }

# Resolve "tool:version" argument → sets TOOL_NAME and TOOL_VERSION
parse_tool_arg() {
  local arg="$1"
  TOOL_NAME="${arg%%:*}"
  TOOL_VERSION="${arg#*:}"
  [ "${TOOL_VERSION}" = "${TOOL_NAME}" ] && TOOL_VERSION=""  # no colon → empty
}

# Auto-init or sync the CodeGraph index in the current git repository.
# If .codegraph/ already exists (restored from cache) → sync.
# If not → init non-interactively.
# Skips silently if not inside a git repository or if codegraph is not installed.
_codegraph_restore_gitignore() {
  local workspace="$1"

  if git -C "${workspace}" ls-files --error-unmatch .codegraph/.gitignore >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    git -C "${workspace}" checkout -- .codegraph/.gitignore >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  else
    rm -f "${workspace}/.codegraph/.gitignore"
  fi
}

# Makes sure the generated CodeGraph index is never version-controlled in the
# target workspace:
#  1. Adds a `.codegraph/` entry to the workspace-root .gitignore (idempotent).
#  2. If the index was already committed by a previous (pre-fix) run, untracks
#     it (git rm --cached) while leaving the files on disk.
# This is what prevents `.codegraph/codegraph.db` from ever showing up as an
# untracked/modified file that can block `git checkout <branch>` or get
# swept into an unrelated auto-commit.
_codegraph_ensure_ignored() {
  local workspace="$1"
  local gitignore="${workspace}/.gitignore"

  if ! git -C "${workspace}" rev-parse --git-dir &>/dev/null 2>&1; then
    return 0
  fi

  if [ ! -f "${gitignore}" ] || ! grep -qxF ".codegraph/" "${gitignore}" 2>/dev/null; then
    { [ -s "${gitignore}" ] && echo ""; echo "# CodeGraph generated index — regenerated per-run, must never be committed"; echo ".codegraph/"; } >> "${gitignore}"
    echo "📝 Added .codegraph/ to workspace .gitignore"
  fi

  if git -C "${workspace}" ls-files --error-unmatch .codegraph >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "🧹 .codegraph/ was previously committed to this repo — untracking it (git rm --cached), keeping files on disk"
    git -C "${workspace}" rm -r --cached .codegraph >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
}

_codegraph_init_or_sync() {
  local workspace="${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-${PWD}}"

  if ! command -v codegraph &>/dev/null; then
    return 0
  fi

  if ! git -C "${workspace}" rev-parse --git-dir &>/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "ℹ️  Not a git repository — skipping CodeGraph init"
    return 0
  fi

  if [ -d "${workspace}/.codegraph" ]; then
    echo "🔄 CodeGraph index found — syncing..."
    codegraph sync "${workspace}" 2>/dev/null || true
    _codegraph_restore_gitignore "${workspace}"
    echo "✅ CodeGraph index synced"
  else
    echo "🔨 Initializing CodeGraph index..."
    codegraph init -i "${workspace}" 2>/dev/null || true
    _codegraph_restore_gitignore "${workspace}"
    echo "✅ CodeGraph index initialized"
  fi

  _codegraph_ensure_ignored "${workspace}"
}

# ── Portable file hashing ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# macOS ships `md5` (BSD) and `shasum`, but not `md5sum`/`sha256sum`.
# Linux ships `md5sum`/`sha256sum` (GNU coreutils), usually not `md5`.
# This helper tries every common tool in order and always returns a value
# (falls back to "nokey" if the file is missing or no hashing tool exists,
# so cache keys never end with a literal empty string).
hash_file() {
  local file="$1"

  if [ ! -f "${file}" ]; then
    echo "nokey"
    return 0
  fi

  if command -v sha256sum &>/dev/null; then
    sha256sum "${file}" | cut -d' ' -f1
  elif command -v shasum &>/dev/null; then
    shasum -a 256 "${file}" | cut -d' ' -f1
  elif command -v md5sum &>/dev/null; then
    md5sum "${file}" | cut -d' ' -f1
  elif command -v md5 &>/dev/null; then
    md5 -q "${file}"
  else
    echo "nokey"
  fi
}

# Hash multiple files together (order-stable, concatenates individual hashes then hashes the result).
hash_files() {
  local combined=""
  for f in "$@"; do
    combined="${combined}$(hash_file "${f}")"
  done
  echo "${combined}" | { command -v sha256sum &>/dev/null && sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1; } \
    || echo "${combined}" | { command -v shasum &>/dev/null && shasum -a 256 | cut -d' ' -f1; } \
    || echo "${combined}"
}

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write

## Usage

```bash
warmup-session.sh --repo <git-url> --dir <target-dir> [--branch <name>] \
  [--exclude "tool1 tool2 ..."] [--install-args "extra args for install.sh"]
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--repo` | Git URL of the product repo (the one that has `agents` as a submodule). |
| `--dir` | Local directory to clone into (or sync, if it already exists). |
| `--branch` | Checkout/track this branch instead of the repo's default. |
| `--exclude` | Space-separated tool names to skip (forwarded to `install.sh all` as `-tool1 -tool2 ...`). |
| `--install-args` | Extra raw arguments appended to the `install.sh` invocation. |

Idempotent: re-running against an existing `--dir` does `git fetch` + `checkout` +
`pull --ff-only` + `submodule update --init --recursive` instead of cloning again, so the
same command works for both first-time warmup and later re-warmups.

## Cloud dev-environment templates (e.g. Bitrise Dev Environments)

Most cloud dev-environment products split session bootstrap into a **warmup** script
(runs once, when the session is first created — good place for the heavy clone +
toolchain install) and a **startup** script (runs on every session start/restart — keep
this fast, just a repo sync).

**Warmup script field:**

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Private repo: a fresh session has no credential helper and no TTY, so a
# plain `git clone https://github.com/...` fails with "could not read
# Username ... Device not configured". Authenticate before the FIRST clone
# (warmup-session.sh itself repeats this line internally for everything it
# clones/fetches afterwards, but that's too late for this bootstrap clone).
# Skip this line entirely if your-org/your-product-repo is public.
git config --global url."https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/".insteadOf "https://github.com/"

git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/your-org/your-product-repo.git repo
bash repo/agents/scripts/warmup-session.sh \
  --repo https://github.com/your-org/your-product-repo.git \
  --dir repo \
  --branch main \
  --exclude "cursor codemie kimi maestro playwright"
```

(The first `git clone` bootstraps the directory so `agents/scripts/warmup-session.sh`
exists to call; the script itself is idempotent, so this is safe even though it clones
twice on a truly fresh session.)

**Startup script field** (every session start/restart — just sync, no reinstall):

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Needed again here for private repos: the `git config --global` from the
# warmup script only persists if the session's home directory is on a
# persistent disk carried over between starts. Setting it unconditionally in
# both scripts is cheap and avoids depending on that persistence guarantee.
git config --global url."https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/".insteadOf "https://github.com/"

cd repo
git fetch origin
git checkout main
git pull --ff-only origin main
git submodule update --init --recursive
```

**Template variables** (mark secrets as *Secret* + *Expose as env var*, so they land as
real environment variables the AI agent scripts pick up directly):

- `JIRA_EMAIL`, `JIRA_API_TOKEN` (secret)
- `GH_TOKEN` / `PAT_TOKEN` — needs push access to `your-org/your-product-repo` (secret)
- `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` (or whatever `AI_AGENT_PROVIDER` your project uses needs) (secret)
- `JIRA_BASE_PATH`, `JIRA_AUTH_TYPE`, `CONFLUENCE_BASE_PATH`, `AI_AGENT_PROVIDER`,
  `COPILOT_MODEL` — not secret, fine as plain template variables

## GitHub Codespaces / `devcontainer.json`

Codespaces has the same two-phase model: `onCreateCommand` (once, at container creation —
equivalent to "warmup") and `postStartCommand` (every start — equivalent to "startup").
Codespaces already checks out the repo itself, so there's no need to `git clone` — just
init submodules and run the script against the existing checkout.

```jsonc
// .devcontainer/devcontainer.json
{
  "name": "your-product-repo",
  "image": "mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/base:ubuntu",
  "onCreateCommand": "git submodule update --init --recursive && bash agents/scripts/warmup-session.sh --repo https://github.com/your-org/your-product-repo.git --dir . --branch main --exclude \"cursor codemie kimi maestro playwright\"",
  "postStartCommand": "git fetch origin && git submodule update --init --recursive"
}
```

Secrets go in **Codespaces → Repository/Organization secrets** (Settings → Secrets and
variables → Codespaces) with the same names as above — GitHub injects them as real
environment variables into every Codespace automatically, so no extra wiring is needed
beyond naming them consistently with what `run-agent.sh` / `run-teammate-local.sh`
expect.

## PR Description

Closes #918
### Root Cause

Factory legs (dev/review/rework) on Dart repos run with no Dart SDK — hosted runner images ship no `dart` and the factory setup layer had no Dart provisioner — so a rework leg cannot run `dart analyze`/`dart test`/`dart format`/`crap4dart check` and claims success while CRAP/method_size/format violations stay in place (#408, #413, #414).

### Fix

- `setup/dart.sh` (new): cached, channel-aware Dart SDK provisioner — same pattern as the golden-test Flutter toolchain for fa legs. Resolves the target like CI: argument/`DART_VERSION` env → the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `sdk:`/`channel:` in the repo's own quality workflow ("same channel the repo's quality.yml uses") → `stable`; downloads from the same dart-archive CDN; installs under `~/.dart-sdk/dart-sdk`; puts `bin` on PATH for the leg session + exports `DART_HOME`/`DART_VERSION`; version-aware reinstall on mismatch (persistent pool-VM `$HOME`).
- `setup/install.sh` / `setup/cache.sh`: `dart` wired into the tool list, PATH verification, and `DART_CACHE_*` cache key/path.
- Docs: `docs/machine-factory-integration.md` (corrected the false "dart from the runner image" claim, `DART_VERSION` var row), `README.md`, `scripts/warmup-session.md`. Dart-repo runners opt in via `customParams.setupCommands: ["bash agents/setup/dart.sh"]`.

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js` (new, in `run_all.json`): 13 hermetic tests — resolution precedence, dart-archive URL/os-arch mapping, `dart-sdk/bin` PATH layout, banner parsing, `install.sh`/`cache.sh` wiring contracts. RED first (12 failing pre-fix), GREEN after.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2843 passed, 0 failed.
- Live on the runner: `setup/dart.sh` installed stable 3.13.5; second run = version-aware cache hit; `setup/install.sh dart` PATH verification green.

### Notes

- Non-dart repos unaffected; `DART_CACHE_*` keys the CI cache. No workflow/dispatch changes — the fix lands entirely in the setup layer this repo owns.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #920._

> ℹ️ **2 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `setup/dart.sh`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-16):
🚨 **BLOCKING: version-aware cache hit never fires on beta/dev channels — SDK is wiped and re-downloaded on every leg**

`channel_latest` resolves the **full** version string from the dart-archive `VERSION` file, but `installed_version` truncates the `dart --version` banner at the first `-`:

```bash
# channel_latest → 3.14.0-315.1.beta   (current live beta VERSION file)
"${d}" --version 2>&1 \
  | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([0-9][0-9.]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
# → 3.14.0   (capture stops at '-'; banner is: Dart SDK version: 3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) ...)
```

Verified against the live dart-archive: `channels/beta/release/latest/VERSION` → `3.14.0-315.1.beta`, `channels/dev/...` → `3.15.0-27.0.dev`. So for any repo whose quality.yml pins `channel: beta`/`dev` — exactly the "same channel the repo's quality.yml uses" case this PR advertises and its own tests resolve against — `have != resolved` is **always true** in `do_install`:

- the CI cache restores the SDK, `dart.sh` declares a mismatch, `rm -rf "${DART_INSTALL_DIR}"`s it and re-downloads ~215 MB + re-extracts **on every leg** — the ticket's "cached dart SDK" is defeated for non-stable channels (the live "second run = version-aware cache hit" validation only covered stable);
- `export_dart_env "$(installed_version)"` exports the **truncated** `DART_VERSION=3.14.0` to `GITHUB_ENV`, which a later `setup/cache.sh save dart` then keys on (`dart-3.14.0-...`), so the save key never matches the restore key (`dart-stable-...`) either — see also the cache.sh comment.

Fix (one line) — capture the full version token:

[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]
| sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
```

The new suite can catch this: the stub-dart mechanism already exists — add
`dsRun('status', { stubDart: 'Dart SDK version: 3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) on "linux_x64"' })`
asserting `installed === '3.14.0-315.1.beta'` (RED today).

Related, same function: a **foreign** PATH dart (not the one this script installed) that happens to match `resolved` also takes the cache-hit branch, registering a possibly nonexistent `${SDK_BIN}` on PATH and pointing `DART_HOME` at it. Prefer probing `${SDK_BIN}/dart` (the managed install) before `command -v dart`, or verify `${SDK_BIN}/dart` exists before the cache-hit early-return.

---

### Thread 2 — `setup/cache.sh`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-16):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `DART_CACHE_KEY` doesn't follow the target `dart.sh` actually resolves — save/restore keys can never round-trip**

`_cache_dart` keys on `${1:-${DART_VERSION:-stable}}` — the `DART_VERSION` **env var** or the literal `stable` — but `dart.sh` resolves its target from the repo's quality.yml (`sdk:`/`channel:`) when the env is unset. On a beta-pinned repo (or one with an `sdk:` pin):

- the **restore** step (`cache.sh keys dart` before install) exports `DART_CACHE_KEY=dart-stable-<os>` while the SDK that gets installed is beta;

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the Dart SDK — cached, channel-aware provisioner for machine-factory
# leg sessions (gh-918).
#
# WHY: factory legs (dev/review/rework) on Dart repos had NO dart SDK on PATH —
# they could not run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check`, so they
# could neither see nor verify quality-gate violations (CRAP / method_size /
# format) and claimed success while violations stayed in place. Same pattern
# as the golden-test Flutter toolchain for fa legs: the SDK is cached per
# resolved version and exposed on PATH for the leg session, resolving the SAME
# channel (and pinned version, when CI pins one) the checked-out repo's
# quality workflow uses — the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `channel:`/`sdk:`
# inputs in `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The SDK itself downloads from the same
# dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart` uses, so leg-local gate output
# matches CI gate output.
#
# Version-aware like setup/fa.sh: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on
# mismatch — pool VMs keep a PERSISTENT $HOME, so a presence-only check lets
# an ancient binary shadow the requested toolchain forever.
#
# Usage:
#   dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]  # default: dart-lang/setup-dart detection, else stable
#   DART_VERSION=beta dart.sh
#   DART_INSTALL_DIR=... dart.sh         # default: ~/.dart-sdk (SDK lands at <dir>/dart-sdk)
#
# Network-free subcommands (unit-test surface — js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js):
#   dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|<version>]
#       print the resolved target/URL/layout as key=value — no download
#   dart.sh status
#       print installed=<version from the dart --version banner> ('' when absent)
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/_common.sh"

DART_ARCHIVE="https://storage.googleapis.com/dart-archive"
DART_INSTALL_DIR="${DART_INSTALL_DIR:-${HOME}/.dart-sdk}"
SDK_HOME="${DART_INSTALL_DIR}/dart-sdk"
SDK_BIN="${SDK_HOME}/bin"

# ── Platform ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# dart-archive bundle naming: dartsdk-<os>-<arch>-release.zip (x64/arm64).
os_arch() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) OS="macos" ;;
    Linux)  OS="linux" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported OS ($(uname -s)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    arm64|aarch64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
    x86_64)        ARCH="x64" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported arch ($(uname -m)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
}

# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Checks PATH first, then
# our own install dir — a cache-restored SDK is real even before its bin dir
# is registered on PATH.
installed_version() {
  local d=""
  if command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    d="$(command -v dart)"
  elif [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
  fi
  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([0-9][0-9.]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# Latest concrete version of a channel (dart-lang/setup-dart resolves "latest"
# through the same VERSION file).
channel_latest() {
  curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/$1/release/latest/VERSION" \
    | sed -n 's/.*"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# ── Quality-workflow detection ("same channel the repo's quality.yml uses") ──
# Scan the checked-out repo's workflows for the dart-lang/setup-dart step and
# read its with: inputs. Echoes "found|sdk|channel" (any field may be empty).
quality_detection() {
  local f kv found=0 sdk="" channel=""
  for f in "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yml "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yaml; do
    [ -f "${f}" ] || continue
    while IFS= read -r kv; do
      case "${kv}" in
        step=*)    found=1 ;;
        sdk=*)     if [ -n "${kv#sdk=}" ] && [ -z "${sdk}" ]; then sdk="${kv#sdk=}"; found=1; fi ;;
        channel=*) if [ -n "${kv#channel=}" ] && [ -z "${channel}" ]; then channel="${kv#channel=}"; found=1; fi ;;
      esac
    done <<EOF
$(awk -v sq="'" '
  /uses:[[:space:]]*dart-lang\/setup-dart/ { inb = 1; print "step=1"; next }
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*(name|uses|run):[[:space:]]/ { inb = 0 }
  inb && /sdk:/ {
    sub(/.*sdk:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "sdk=" $0
  }
  inb && /channel:/ {
    sub(/.*channel:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "channel=" $0
  }
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
EOF
  done
  echo "${found}|${sdk}|${channel}"
}

# ── Target resolution ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Precedence (sets TARGET/MODE/CHANNEL/VERSION/SOURCE):
#   1. explicit argument           → source=argument
#   2. DART_VERSION env            → source=environment
#   3. quality.yml sdk:/channel:   → source=quality workflow
#   4. stable                      → source=default
# A pinned version rides the DETECTED channel (setup-dart keeps using the
# channel for a full version), so leg output keeps matching CI exactly.
resolve_target() {
  local arg="${1:-}"
  TARGET="${arg:-${DART_VERSION:-}}"
  SOURCE="default"
  if [ -n "${arg}" ]; then
    SOURCE="argument"
  elif [ -n "${DART_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    SOURCE="environment"
  fi

  local det found det_sdk det_channel
  det="$(quality_detection)"
  found="${det%%|*}"; det="${det#*|}"
  det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"

  if [ -z "${TARGET}" ]; then
    [ "${found}" = "1" ] && SOURCE="quality workflow"
    # A quality-workflow `sdk:` pin IS a target — the leg runs the exact
    # version CI runs; its `channel:` (or stable) then carries the download.
    [ -n "${det_sdk}" ] && TARGET="${det_sdk}"
  fi

  case "${TARGET}" in
    ""|latest|stable|beta|dev)
      MODE="channel"
      CHANNEL="${TARGET}"
      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ] || [ "${CHANNEL}" = "latest" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_channel}"; fi
      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_sdk:+stable}"; fi
      [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ] && CHANNEL="stable"
      case "${CHANNEL}" in stable|beta|dev) ;; *) CHANNEL="stable" ;; esac
      VERSION=""
      ;;
    *)
      MODE="version"
      VERSION="${TARGET}"
      CHANNEL="${det_channel}"
      [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ] && CHANNEL="stable"
      case "${CHANNEL}" in stable|beta|dev) ;; *) CHANNEL="stable" ;; esac
      ;;
  esac
}

# dart-archive release URL. Channel mode resolves to `latest` until the
# concrete version is fetched at install time.
sdk_url() {
  local ver="${1:-${VERSION:-latest}}"
  [ -n "${ver}" ] || ver="latest"
  echo "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/${CHANNEL}/release/${ver}/sdk/dartsdk-${OS}-${ARCH}-release.zip"
}

print_plan() {
  if [ "${MODE}" = "version" ]; then
    echo "requested=${VERSION}"
  else
    echo "requested=${CHANNEL}"
  fi
  echo "mode=${MODE}"
  echo "channel=${CHANNEL}"
  echo "version=${VERSION:-latest}"
  echo "source=${SOURCE}"
  echo "install_dir=${DART_INSTALL_DIR}"
  echo "sdk_home=${SDK_HOME}"
  echo "sdk_bin_dir=${SDK_BIN}"
  echo "sdk_url=$(sdk_url)"
  echo "register_path=${SDK_BIN}"
}

# ── Install ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
extract_zip() {
  if command -v unzip >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    unzip -q "$1" -d "$2"
  elif [ "$(detect_os)" = "macos" ] && command -v ditto >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ditto -x -k "$1" "$2"
  else
    echo "❌ neither unzip nor ditto available to extract $1" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

export_dart_env() {
  export_var "DART_HOME" "${SDK_HOME}"
  export_var "DART_VERSION" "$1"
}

do_install() {
  echo "🎯 Dart SDK [target=${TARGET:-<detect>} mode=${MODE} channel=${CHANNEL} os=${OS} arch=${ARCH} ci=$(detect_ci)]"

  # Resolve the concrete version for channel mode — it drives BOTH the
  # version-aware cache check below and the cache key.
  local resolved=""
  if [ "${MODE}" = "channel" ]; then
    resolved="$(channel_latest "${CHANNEL}" || true)"
  else
    resolved="${VERSION}"
  fi

  local have
  have="$(installed_version)"

  if [ -n "${resolved}" ] && [ "${have}" = "${resolved}" ]; then

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Common utilities shared by all setup scripts.
# Source this file — do not run it directly.

# ── OS / CI / Package manager detection ──────────────────────────────────────

detect_os() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) echo "macos" ;;
    Linux)  echo "linux" ;;
    *)      echo "unknown" ;;
  esac
}

detect_ci() {
  if   [ -n "${BITRISE_BUILD_NUMBER:-}" ]; then echo "bitrise"
  elif [ -n "${GITHUB_ACTIONS:-}" ];       then echo "github"
  elif [ -n "${BUILD_BUILDID:-}" ];        then echo "ado"
  elif [ -n "${GITLAB_CI:-}" ];            then echo "gitlab"
  else                                          echo "local"
  fi
}

detect_package_manager() {
  if   is_installed brew;    then echo "brew"
  elif is_installed apt-get; then echo "apt"
  else                            echo "none"
  fi
}

# ── PATH / env registration ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Add a directory to PATH — works for the current shell AND subsequent CI steps.
register_path() {
  local dir="$1"
  # Export immediately so the rest of this script can use the binary.
  export PATH="${dir}:${PATH}"

  # Persist to a temp file so parent install.sh can accumulate all paths
  echo "${dir}" >> /tmp/_registered_paths 2>/dev/null || true

  case "$(detect_ci)" in
    bitrise)
      # envman REPLACES the variable — pass the full cumulative PATH.
      command -v envman &>/dev/null \
        && envman add --key PATH --value "${PATH}" \
        || true
      ;;
    github)
      [ -n "${GITHUB_PATH:-}" ] && echo "${dir}" >> "${GITHUB_PATH}" || true
      ;;
    gitlab)
      [ -n "${GITLAB_ENV_PATH:-}" ] && echo "export PATH=\"${dir}:\$PATH\"" >> "${GITLAB_ENV_PATH}" || true
      ;;
    ado)
      echo "##vso[task.prependpath]${dir}"
      ;;
    local) ;;  # already exported above
  esac
}

# Export an env variable so subsequent CI steps can see it.
export_var() {
  local key="$1" value="$2"
  export "${key}=${value}"

  case "$(detect_ci)" in
    bitrise)
      command -v envman &>/dev/null \
        && envman add --key "${key}" --value "${value}" \
        || true
      ;;
    github)
      [ -n "${GITHUB_ENV:-}" ] && echo "${key}=${value}" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}" || true
      ;;
    gitlab)
      [ -n "${GITLAB_ENV_PATH:-}" ] && echo "export ${key}=\"${value}\"" >> "${GITLAB_ENV_PATH}" || true
      ;;
    ado)
      echo "##vso[task.setvariable variable=${key}]${value}"
      ;;
    local) ;;
  esac
}

# ── Helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

is_installed() { command -v "$1" &>/dev/null; }

# Returns "sudo" when not running as root, empty string when already root.
# Usage: $(sudo_cmd) apt-get install ...
sudo_cmd() {
  if [ "$(id -u)" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "sudo"
  else
    echo ""
  fi
}

section() { echo ""; echo "▶ $*"; echo ""; }

# Resolve "tool:version" argument → sets TOOL_NAME and TOOL_VERSION
parse_tool_arg() {
  local arg="$1"
  TOOL_NAME="${arg%%:*}"
  TOOL_VERSION="${arg#*:}"
  [ "${TOOL_VERSION}" = "${TOOL_NAME}" ] && TOOL_VERSION=""  # no colon → empty
}

# Auto-init or sync the CodeGraph index in the current git repository.
# If .codegraph/ already exists (restored from cache) → sync.
# If not → init non-interactively.
# Skips silently if not inside a git repository or if codegraph is not installed.
_codegraph_restore_gitignore() {
  local workspace="$1"

  if git -C "${workspace}" ls-files --error-unmatch .codegraph/.gitignore >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    git -C "${workspace}" checkout -- .codegraph/.gitignore >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  else
    rm -f "${workspace}/.codegraph/.gitignore"
  fi
}

# Makes sure the generated CodeGraph index is never version-controlled in the
# target workspace:
#  1. Adds a `.codegraph/` entry to the workspace-root .gitignore (idempotent).
#  2. If the index was already committed by a previous (pre-fix) run, untracks
#     it (git rm --cached) while leaving the files on disk.
# This is what prevents `.codegraph/codegraph.db` from ever showing up as an
# untracked/modified file that can block `git checkout <branch>` or get
# swept into an unrelated auto-commit.
_codegraph_ensure_ignored() {
  local workspace="$1"
  local gitignore="${workspace}/.gitignore"

  if ! git -C "${workspace}" rev-parse --git-dir &>/dev/null 2>&1; then
    return 0
  fi

  if [ ! -f "${gitignore}" ] || ! grep -qxF ".codegraph/" "${gitignore}" 2>/dev/null; then
    { [ -s "${gitignore}" ] && echo ""; echo "# CodeGraph generated index — regenerated per-run, must never be committed"; echo ".codegraph/"; } >> "${gitignore}"
    echo "📝 Added .codegraph/ to workspace .gitignore"
  fi

  if git -C "${workspace}" ls-files --error-unmatch .codegraph >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "🧹 .codegraph/ was previously committed to this repo — untracking it (git rm --cached), keeping files on disk"
    git -C "${workspace}" rm -r --cached .codegraph >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
}

_codegraph_init_or_sync() {
  local workspace="${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-${PWD}}"

  if ! command -v codegraph &>/dev/null; then
    return 0
  fi

  if ! git -C "${workspace}" rev-parse --git-dir &>/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "ℹ️  Not a git repository — skipping CodeGraph init"
    return 0
  fi

  if [ -d "${workspace}/.codegraph" ]; then
    echo "🔄 CodeGraph index found — syncing..."
    codegraph sync "${workspace}" 2>/dev/null || true
    _codegraph_restore_gitignore "${workspace}"
    echo "✅ CodeGraph index synced"
  else
    echo "🔨 Initializing CodeGraph index..."
    codegraph init -i "${workspace}" 2>/dev/null || true
    _codegraph_restore_gitignore "${workspace}"
    echo "✅ CodeGraph index initialized"
  fi

  _codegraph_ensure_ignored "${workspace}"
}

# ── Portable file hashing ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# macOS ships `md5` (BSD) and `shasum`, but not `md5sum`/`sha256sum`.
# Linux ships `md5sum`/`sha256sum` (GNU coreutils), usually not `md5`.
# This helper tries every common tool in order and always returns a value
# (falls back to "nokey" if the file is missing or no hashing tool exists,
# so cache keys never end with a literal empty string).
hash_file() {
  local file="$1"

  if [ ! -f "${file}" ]; then
    echo "nokey"
    return 0
  fi

  if command -v sha256sum &>/dev/null; then
    sha256sum "${file}" | cut -d' ' -f1
  elif command -v shasum &>/dev/null; then
    shasum -a 256 "${file}" | cut -d' ' -f1
  elif command -v md5sum &>/dev/null; then
    md5sum "${file}" | cut -d' ' -f1
  elif command -v md5 &>/dev/null; then
    md5 -q "${file}"
  else
    echo "nokey"
  fi
}

# Hash multiple files together (order-stable, concatenates individual hashes then hashes the result).
hash_files() {
  local combined=""
  for f in "$@"; do
    combined="${combined}$(hash_file "${f}")"
  done
  echo "${combined}" | { command -v sha256sum &>/dev/null && sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1; } \
    || echo "${combined}" | { command -v shasum &>/dev/null && shasum -a 256 | cut -d' ' -f1; } \
    || echo "${combined}"
}

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write

blocks.text:
## Usage

```bash
warmup-session.sh --repo <git-url> --dir <target-dir> [--branch <name>] \
  [--exclude "tool1 tool2 ..."] [--install-args "extra args for install.sh"]
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--repo` | Git URL of the product repo (the one that has `agents` as a submodule). |
| `--dir` | Local directory to clone into (or sync, if it already exists). |
| `--branch` | Checkout/track this branch instead of the repo's default. |
| `--exclude` | Space-separated tool names to skip (forwarded to `install.sh all` as `-tool1 -tool2 ...`). |
| `--install-args` | Extra raw arguments appended to the `install.sh` invocation. |

Idempotent: re-running against an existing `--dir` does `git fetch` + `checkout` +
`pull --ff-only` + `submodule update --init --recursive` instead of cloning again, so the
same command works for both first-time warmup and later re-warmups.

## Cloud dev-environment templates (e.g. Bitrise Dev Environments)

Most cloud dev-environment products split session bootstrap into a **warmup** script
(runs once, when the session is first created — good place for the heavy clone +
toolchain install) and a **startup** script (runs on every session start/restart — keep
this fast, just a repo sync).

**Warmup script field:**

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Private repo: a fresh session has no credential helper and no TTY, so a
# plain `git clone https://github.com/...` fails with "could not read
# Username ... Device not configured". Authenticate before the FIRST clone
# (warmup-session.sh itself repeats this line internally for everything it
# clones/fetches afterwards, but that's too late for this bootstrap clone).
# Skip this line entirely if your-org/your-product-repo is public.
git config --global url."https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/".insteadOf "https://github.com/"

git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/your-org/your-product-repo.git repo
bash repo/agents/scripts/warmup-session.sh \
  --repo https://github.com/your-org/your-product-repo.git \
  --dir repo \
  --branch main \
  --exclude "cursor codemie kimi maestro playwright"
```

(The first `git clone` bootstraps the directory so `agents/scripts/warmup-session.sh`
exists to call; the script itself is idempotent, so this is safe even though it clones
twice on a truly fresh session.)

**Startup script field** (every session start/restart — just sync, no reinstall):

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Needed again here for private repos: the `git config --global` from the
# warmup script only persists if the session's home directory is on a
# persistent disk carried over between starts. Setting it unconditionally in
# both scripts is cheap and avoids depending on that persistence guarantee.
git config --global url."https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/".insteadOf "https://github.com/"

cd repo
git fetch origin
git checkout main
git pull --ff-only origin main
git submodule update --init --recursive
```

**Template variables** (mark secrets as *Secret* + *Expose as env var*, so they land as
real environment variables the AI agent scripts pick up directly):

- `JIRA_EMAIL`, `JIRA_API_TOKEN` (secret)
- `GH_TOKEN` / `PAT_TOKEN` — needs push access to `your-org/your-product-repo` (secret)
- `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` (or whatever `AI_AGENT_PROVIDER` your project uses needs) (secret)
- `JIRA_BASE_PATH`, `JIRA_AUTH_TYPE`, `CONFLUENCE_BASE_PATH`, `AI_AGENT_PROVIDER`,
  `COPILOT_MODEL` — not secret, fine as plain template variables

## GitHub Codespaces / `devcontainer.json`

Codespaces has the same two-phase model: `onCreateCommand` (once, at container creation —
equivalent to "warmup") and `postStartCommand` (every start — equivalent to "startup").
Codespaces already checks out the repo itself, so there's no need to `git clone` — just
init submodules and run the script against the existing checkout.

```jsonc
// .devcontainer/devcontainer.json
{
  "name": "your-product-repo",
  "image": "mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/base:ubuntu",
  "onCreateCommand": "git submodule update --init --recursive && bash agents/scripts/warmup-session.sh --repo https://github.com/your-org/your-product-repo.git --dir . --branch main --exclude \"cursor codemie kimi maestro playwright\"",

## PR Description

Closes #918
### Root Cause

Factory legs (dev/review/rework) on Dart repos run with no Dart SDK — hosted runner images ship no `dart` and the factory setup layer had no Dart provisioner — so a rework leg cannot run `dart analyze`/`dart test`/`dart format`/`crap4dart check` and claims success while CRAP/method_size/format violations stay in place (#408, #413, #414).

### Fix

- `setup/dart.sh` (new): cached, channel-aware Dart SDK provisioner — same pattern as the golden-test Flutter toolchain for fa legs. Resolves the target like CI: argument/`DART_VERSION` env → the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `sdk:`/`channel:` in the repo's own quality workflow ("same channel the repo's quality.yml uses") → `stable`; downloads from the same dart-archive CDN; installs under `~/.dart-sdk/dart-sdk`; puts `bin` on PATH for the leg session + exports `DART_HOME`/`DART_VERSION`; version-aware reinstall on mismatch (persistent pool-VM `$HOME`).
- `setup/install.sh` / `setup/cache.sh`: `dart` wired into the tool list, PATH verification, and `DART_CACHE_*` cache key/path.
- Docs: `docs/machine-factory-integration.md` (corrected the false "dart from the runner image" claim, `DART_VERSION` var row), `README.md`, `scripts/warmup-session.md`. Dart-repo runners opt in via `customParams.setupCommands: ["bash agents/setup/dart.sh"]`.

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js` (new, in `run_all.json`): 13 hermetic tests — resolution precedence, dart-archive URL/os-arch mapping, `dart-sdk/bin` PATH layout, banner parsing, `install.sh`/`cache.sh` wiring contracts. RED first (12 failing pre-fix), GREEN after.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2843 passed, 0 failed.
- Live on the runner: `setup/dart.sh` installed stable 3.13.5; second run = version-aware cache hit; `setup/install.sh dart` PATH verification green.

### Notes

- Non-dart repos unaffected; `DART_CACHE_*` keys the CI cache. No workflow/dispatch changes — the fix lands entirely in the setup layer this repo owns.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #920._

> ℹ️ **2 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `setup/dart.sh`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-16):
🚨 **BLOCKING: version-aware cache hit never fires on beta/dev channels — SDK is wiped and re-downloaded on every leg**

`channel_latest` resolves the **full** version string from the dart-archive `VERSION` file, but `installed_version` truncates the `dart --version` banner at the first `-`:

```bash
# channel_latest → 3.14.0-315.1.beta   (current live beta VERSION file)
"${d}" --version 2>&1 \
  | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([0-9][0-9.]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
# → 3.14.0   (capture stops at '-'; banner is: Dart SDK version: 3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) ...)
```

Verified against the live dart-archive: `channels/beta/release/latest/VERSION` → `3.14.0-315.1.beta`, `channels/dev/...` → `3.15.0-27.0.dev`. So for any repo whose quality.yml pins `channel: beta`/`dev` — exactly the "same channel the repo's quality.yml uses" case this PR advertises and its own tests resolve against — `have != resolved` is **always true** in `do_install`:

- the CI cache restores the SDK, `dart.sh` declares a mismatch, `rm -rf "${DART_INSTALL_DIR}"`s it and re-downloads ~215 MB + re-extracts **on every leg** — the ticket's "cached dart SDK" is defeated for non-stable channels (the live "second run = version-aware cache hit" validation only covered stable);
- `export_dart_env "$(installed_version)"` exports the **truncated** `DART_VERSION=3.14.0` to `GITHUB_ENV`, which a later `setup/cache.sh save dart` then keys on (`dart-3.14.0-...`), so the save key never matches the restore key (`dart-stable-...`) either — see also the cache.sh comment.

Fix (one line) — capture the full version token:

[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]
| sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
```

The new suite can catch this: the stub-dart mechanism already exists — add
`dsRun('status', { stubDart: 'Dart SDK version: 3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) on "linux_x64"' })`
asserting `installed === '3.14.0-315.1.beta'` (RED today).

Related, same function: a **foreign** PATH dart (not the one this script installed) that happens to match `resolved` also takes the cache-hit branch, registering a possibly nonexistent `${SDK_BIN}` on PATH and pointing `DART_HOME` at it. Prefer probing `${SDK_BIN}/dart` (the managed install) before `command -v dart`, or verify `${SDK_BIN}/dart` exists before the cache-hit early-return.

---

### Thread 2 — `setup/cache.sh`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-16):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `DART_CACHE_KEY` doesn't follow the target `dart.sh` actually resolves — save/restore keys can never round-trip**

`_cache_dart` keys on `${1:-${DART_VERSION:-stable}}` — the `DART_VERSION` **env var** or the literal `stable` — but `dart.sh` resolves its target from the repo's quality.yml (`sdk:`/`channel:`) when the env is unset. On a beta-pinned repo (or one with an `sdk:` pin):

- the **restore** step (`cache.sh keys dart` before install) exports `DART_CACHE_KEY=dart-stable-<os>` while the SDK that gets installed is beta;
- the **save** step (after install) sees `DART_VERSION` re-exported by `dart.sh` (via `GITHUB_ENV`) set to the installed version, so it saves under `dart-<installed>-<os>` — a key the restore step never looked for. The primary key can never hit; only the `dart-` restore-key fallback keeps the cache functional.

So the doc comment above ("Key on the requested channel/version") and the README/docs claim "cache it per resolved version" don't hold — the key tracks the env var, not the resolution. Suggested alignment (pick one):

1. have `cache.sh` resolve the same way `dart.sh` does — e.g. `requested="$(bash "${SCRIPT_DIR}/dart.sh" plan | sed -n 's/^requested=//p')"` — and key on that;
2. or stop re-exporting `DART_VERSION` from `dart.sh` / have `cache.sh` ignore it, and document the required step ordering (keys → restore → install → save with an explicit version).

As-is it works by accident of the restore-key fallback and self-heals via the version-aware reinstall — but the PR's own docs promise the primary key tracks the resolved target, and it doesn't.

---

### Thread 3 — `setup/dart.sh`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-16):
💡 **SUGGESTION: verify the downloaded SDK archive (sha256 sidecar exists) and harden the big fetch**

Two hardening nits on the ~215 MB toolchain download:

1. dart-archive publishes a `.sha256` next to every bundle (`dartsdk-<os>-<arch>-release.zip.sha256`), and `_common.sh` already ships `hash_file`. Verifying after download is cheap supply-chain insurance for a script that runs on every Dart-repo leg:

```bash
curl -fsSL "${url}.sha256" -o "${tmp}/dartsdk.zip.sha256"
echo "$(cat "${tmp}/dartsdk.zip.sha256")  ${tmp}/dartsdk.zip" | (command -v sha256sum >/dev/null && sha256sum -c - || shasum -a 256 -c -)
```

2. `channel_latest` gets `--max-time 30`, but the main download has no timeout/retry at all — a stalled transfer hangs the leg until the workflow-level timeout. `--connect-timeout 30 --retry 3 --retry-delay 5` costs nothing.

Minor: on curl failure the `mktemp -d` dir leaks (no `trap`); consider `trap 'rm -rf "${tmp}"' EXIT` or moving cleanup into an EXIT trap.

---

### Thread 4 — `setup/dart.sh`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-16):
💡 **SUGGESTION: a mistyped first argument silently becomes a version target**

The default branch feeds `CMD` straight into `resolve_target`, so `dart.sh --help`, `dart.sh instal`, `dart.sh v3.9.4` (note the `v` — dart-archive URLs are unprefixed) all resolve to *version mode* and fail much later as a bare `curl` 404 on `.../release/--help/sdk/dartsdk-...zip`, which reads like a network/CDN problem rather than a usage error.

Verify live today:

```
$ dart.sh plan --help
requested=--help
mode=version
version=--help
```

Suggest validating the target up front in `resolve_target` (or the main `case`) and printing usage on garbage:

```bash
case "${TARGET}" in
  ""|latest|stable|beta|dev) ;;
  [0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*) ;;                       # 3.9.4 / 3.14.0-315.1.beta
  *) echo "❌ unknown target '${TARGET}' (stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>)" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac
```

(Arguably also accept a leading `v` by stripping it — `install.sh` peers like `fa.sh`/`dmtools.sh` pin with `v`-prefixed tags, so muscle memory will try `v` here too.)

---

### Thread 5 — `setup/dart.sh`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-16):
💡 **SUGGESTION: quality.yml detection misses quoted `uses:` and commented-out steps**

Two robustness gaps in the `awk` scanner:

1. A quoted action ref — `uses: "dart-lang/setup-dart@v1"` (legal YAML, shows up in generated/templated workflows) — doesn't match `/uses:[[:space:]]*dart-lang\/setup-dart/`, so detection silently falls back to stable while CI runs another channel. Allowing an optional `"` before the ref covers it: `/uses:[[:space:]]*"?(dart-lang\/setup-dart)/`.
2. A commented-out step line (`# - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1`) *does* match, and its following comment lines can contribute bogus `sdk:`/`channel:` values. Anchoring `uses:` to the start of a list item (`/^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*uses:...`) or skipping lines whose first non-space char is `#` would remove both false directions.

Low probability inputs, high-value output (this decides which toolchain every leg runs) — worth the two extra character classes. The existing fixtures in `test_dartSetup.js` are a good place for the two negative/quoted cases.

---

### Thread 6 — `setup/install.sh`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-16):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `install.sh all` now pulls the Dart SDK on every consumer, including non-Dart repos**

Adding `dart` to `ALL_TOOLS` means `install.sh all` — which `scripts/warmup-session.sh` runs for **any** target repo (Codespaces / dev-container bootstrap) — now downloads the ~215 MB zip and installs ~1 GB under `~/.dart-sdk` on every warmup of a non-Dart repo too. The PR notes "Non-dart repos unaffected"; that holds for the factory legs (they opt in via `customParams.setupCommands`), but not for `install.sh all` / warmup users, who now pay the cost unless they know to pass `--exclude dart`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the Dart SDK — cached, channel-aware provisioner for machine-factory
# leg sessions (gh-918).
#
# WHY: factory legs (dev/review/rework) on Dart repos had NO dart SDK on PATH —
# they could not run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check`, so they
# could neither see nor verify quality-gate violations (CRAP / method_size /
# format) and claimed success while violations stayed in place. Same pattern
# as the golden-test Flutter toolchain for fa legs: the SDK is cached per
# resolved version and exposed on PATH for the leg session, resolving the SAME
# channel (and pinned version, when CI pins one) the checked-out repo's
# quality workflow uses — the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `channel:`/`sdk:`
# inputs in `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The SDK itself downloads from the same
# dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart` uses, so leg-local gate output
# matches CI gate output.
#
# Version-aware like setup/fa.sh: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on
# mismatch — pool VMs keep a PERSISTENT $HOME, so a presence-only check lets
# an ancient binary shadow the requested toolchain forever.
#
# Usage:
#   dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]  # default: dart-lang/setup-dart detection, else stable
#   DART_VERSION=beta dart.sh
#   DART_INSTALL_DIR=... dart.sh         # default: ~/.dart-sdk (SDK lands at <dir>/dart-sdk)
#
# Network-free subcommands (unit-test surface — js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js):
#   dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|<version>]
#       print the resolved target/URL/layout as key=value — no download
#   dart.sh status
#       print installed=<version from the dart --version banner> ('' when absent)
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/_common.sh"

DART_ARCHIVE="https://storage.googleapis.com/dart-archive"
DART_INSTALL_DIR="${DART_INSTALL_DIR:-${HOME}/.dart-sdk}"
SDK_HOME="${DART_INSTALL_DIR}/dart-sdk"
SDK_BIN="${SDK_HOME}/bin"

# ── Platform ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# dart-archive bundle naming: dartsdk-<os>-<arch>-release.zip (x64/arm64).
os_arch() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) OS="macos" ;;
    Linux)  OS="linux" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported OS ($(uname -s)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    arm64|aarch64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
    x86_64)        ARCH="x64" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported arch ($(uname -m)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
}

# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Checks PATH first, then
# our own install dir — a cache-restored SDK is real even before its bin dir
# is registered on PATH.
installed_version() {
  local d=""
  if command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    d="$(command -v dart)"
  elif [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
  fi
  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([0-9][0-9.]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# Latest concrete version of a channel (dart-lang/setup-dart resolves "latest"
# through the same VERSION file).
channel_latest() {
  curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/$1/release/latest/VERSION" \
    | sed -n 's/.*"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# ── Quality-workflow detection ("same channel the repo's quality.yml uses") ──
# Scan the checked-out repo's workflows for the dart-lang/setup-dart step and
# read its with: inputs. Echoes "found|sdk|channel" (any field may be empty).
quality_detection() {
  local f kv found=0 sdk="" channel=""
  for f in "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yml "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yaml; do
    [ -f "${f}" ] || continue
    while IFS= read -r kv; do
      case "${kv}" in
        step=*)    found=1 ;;
        sdk=*)     if [ -n "${kv#sdk=}" ] && [ -z "${sdk}" ]; then sdk="${kv#sdk=}"; found=1; fi ;;
        channel=*) if [ -n "${kv#channel=}" ] && [ -z "${channel}" ]; then channel="${kv#channel=}"; found=1; fi ;;
      esac
    done <<EOF
$(awk -v sq="'" '
  /uses:[[:space:]]*dart-lang\/setup-dart/ { inb = 1; print "step=1"; next }
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*(name|uses|run):[[:space:]]/ { inb = 0 }
  inb && /sdk:/ {
    sub(/.*sdk:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "sdk=" $0
  }
  inb && /channel:/ {
    sub(/.*channel:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "channel=" $0
  }
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
EOF
  done
  echo "${found}|${sdk}|${channel}"
}

# ── Target resolution ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Precedence (sets TARGET/MODE/CHANNEL/VERSION/SOURCE):
#   1. explicit argument           → source=argument
#   2. DART_VERSION env            → source=environment
#   3. quality.yml sdk:/channel:   → source=quality workflow
#   4. stable                      → source=default
# A pinned version rides the DETECTED channel (setup-dart keeps using the
# channel for a full version), so leg output keeps matching CI exactly.
resolve_target() {
  local arg="${1:-}"
  TARGET="${arg:-${DART_VERSION:-}}"
  SOURCE="default"
  if [ -n "${arg}" ]; then
    SOURCE="argument"
  elif [ -n "${DART_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    SOURCE="environment"
  fi

  local det found det_sdk det_channel
  det="$(quality_detection)"
  found="${det%%|*}"; det="${det#*|}"
  det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"

  if [ -z "${TARGET}" ]; then
    [ "${found}" = "1" ] && SOURCE="quality workflow"
    # A quality-workflow `sdk:` pin IS a target — the leg runs the exact
    # version CI runs; its `channel:` (or stable) then carries the download.
    [ -n "${det_sdk}" ] && TARGET="${det_sdk}"
  fi

  case "${TARGET}" in
    ""|latest|stable|beta|dev)
      MODE="channel"
      CHANNEL="${TARGET}"
      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ] || [ "${CHANNEL}" = "latest" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_channel}"; fi
      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_sdk:+stable}"; fi
      [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ] && CHANNEL="stable"
      case "${CHANNEL}" in stable|beta|dev) ;; *) CHANNEL="stable" ;; esac
      VERSION=""
      ;;
    *)
      MODE="version"
      VERSION="${TARGET}"
      CHANNEL="${det_channel}"
      [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ] && CHANNEL="stable"
      case "${CHANNEL}" in stable|beta|dev) ;; *) CHANNEL="stable" ;; esac
      ;;
  esac
}

# dart-archive release URL. Channel mode resolves to `latest` until the
# concrete version is fetched at install time.
sdk_url() {
  local ver="${1:-${VERSION:-latest}}"
  [ -n "${ver}" ] || ver="latest"
  echo "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/${CHANNEL}/release/${ver}/sdk/dartsdk-${OS}-${ARCH}-release.zip"
}

print_plan() {
  if [ "${MODE}" = "version" ]; then
    echo "requested=${VERSION}"
  else
    echo "requested=${CHANNEL}"
  fi
  echo "mode=${MODE}"
  echo "channel=${CHANNEL}"
  echo "version=${VERSION:-latest}"
  echo "source=${SOURCE}"
  echo "install_dir=${DART_INSTALL_DIR}"
  echo "sdk_home=${SDK_HOME}"
  echo "sdk_bin_dir=${SDK_BIN}"
  echo "sdk_url=$(sdk_url)"
  echo "register_path=${SDK_BIN}"
}

# ── Install ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
extract_zip() {
  if command -v unzip >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    unzip -q "$1" -d "$2"
  elif [ "$(detect_os)" = "macos" ] && command -v ditto >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ditto -x -k "$1" "$2"
  else
    echo "❌ neither unzip nor ditto available to extract $1" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

export_dart_env() {
  export_var "DART_HOME" "${SDK_HOME}"
  export_var "DART_VERSION" "$1"
}

do_install() {
  echo "🎯 Dart SDK [target=${TARGET:-<detect>} mode=${MODE} channel=${CHANNEL} os=${OS} arch=${ARCH} ci=$(detect_ci)]"

  # Resolve the concrete version for channel mode — it drives BOTH the
  # version-aware cache check below and the cache key.
  local resolved=""
  if [ "${MODE}" = "channel" ]; then
    resolved="$(channel_latest "${CHANNEL}" || true)"
  else
    resolved="${VERSION}"
  fi

  local have
  have="$(installed_version)"

  if [ -n "${resolved}" ] && [ "${have}" = "${resolved}" ]; then
